_exec_summary.SummaryText:
Air Products LLC (LaPorte)

1.  Accidental release prevention and emergency response policies:

At this facility, we manufacture gaseous hydrogen.  Hydrogen and methane, in the amounts handled by our facility, is considered hazardous by the EPA.   It is our policy to adhere to all applicable Federal and state rules and regulations.  Air Products manages the safety of the regulated processes by means of operating procedures, equipment testing and inspections, safety devices (e.g., alarms, shutdowns, instrumentation, relief devices) inherent in the design of this facility and other controls and systems designed to prevent accidental releases of hazardous chemicals.  Safe work practices and training of our personnel supplement the inherent safe design of the plant.

This document has been prepared in accordance with the EPAs Risk Management Plan regulation (40 CFR, Part 68). The substances and processes considered during the preparation of this RMP and the scenarios described were selected based on criteria established in the regulation.

2.  The stationary source and regulated substances handled:

Process Description: There are two processing units on site.  For the gasifier process, natural gas and oxygen are received by our plant via pipelines and used as feedstock.  The oxygen and natural gas are combined in the gasifier, in a process called partial oxidation reaction.  The partial oxidation process is a process where oxygen and natural gas are injected through a burner into a hot refractory lined gasifier.  The oxygen and natural gas are converted in the gasifier at 2500 F to syngas.  Syngas consists mainly of hydrogen and carbon monoxide.  Carbon dioxide and steam are also produced in the partial oxidation process.  Carbon dioxide is removed from the syngas by flowing through a scrubber.  The syngas is dried to remove moisture, then separated into hydrogen and carbon monoxide through a cryogenic distillation process.  The hydrogen is sent through a pressure swing

adsorber to remove residual carbon monoxide.  The pure hydrogen is then compressed and delivered to our customers via pipelines or filled into tube trailers.  Back up hydrogen is provided by a liquid hydrogen storage tank and gaseous hydrogen storage tube banks.  The CO2 Reforming Process uses Natural Gas, Carbon Dioxide, Steam and Oxygen as feedstock.  These are reacted in a process called CO2 reforming.  This results in a mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide.  This mixture is purified to produce pure hydrogen and carbon monoxide which are the main products for the CO2 reforming process unit. The hydrogen and carbon monoxide are delivered to our customers via pipeline or tube trailers.

3.  The general accidental release prevention program and specific prevention steps:

The facility developed prevention program elements based on the Federal EPA Accidental Release Prevention Plan and OSHA Process Safety Management (PSM) regulations.  This facility was designed and constructed to comply with applicable state and industry codes.

4.  Five-year accident history:

There have been no accidents involving or accidental releases of flammable gas that resulted in any deaths, injuries, or significant property damage on site, or known off-site deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage.

5.  The emergency response program:

The facility emergency response program is based upon OSHAs HAZWOPER standard.  At this site, employees are trained to recognize emergencies and initiate emergency response from outside agencies.  They are trained to OSHA First Responder Awareness (FRA) Level.  The employees receive annual refresher training in their role in the emergency plan.  Emergency response activities are conducted for emergencies related to the hydrogen process.  In addition, periodic drills are offered for local emergency response agencies to participate and review the effectiveness of our emergency procedures.
